name: PESTEL Analysis
use_case: A scan of the macro-environment surrounding an organisation across six external forces it cannot control: political, economic, social, technological, environmental and legal. Best used before a long-horizon commitment such as entering a country, planning a multi-year investment or reviewing regulatory exposure, when the risks that matter originate outside the industry entirely and would otherwise never come up in a competitor-focused discussion.
strengths: covers forces outside the industry that competitor analysis never reaches
the six prompts reliably surface regulatory and demographic blind spots
well suited to long horizons where the macro picture dominates
output feeds directly into scenario planning
weaknesses: produces a long list with no weighting or probability
goes stale quickly in volatile political or regulatory environments
tempts teams into cataloguing headlines rather than analysing impact
says nothing about what the organisation should actually do
use_cases: A ministry's policy team is starting a horizon scan and needs a structured way to sort the political, social, technological, legal and environmental changes that could affect the programme it runs.
A university's leadership wants to understand how shifts in government funding, student visa rules, inflation and sustainability expectations will affect enrolment and budgets in the coming years.
A manufacturer faces new carbon-disclosure rules, rising energy prices and an ageing workforce, and its leadership wants to see which of these outside pressures matter most for its operations.
A regional health authority wants to anticipate how an ageing population, new data-protection law and changing government priorities will shape demand for its services.
